LESSON: GUIDED WRITING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Writing 3.6 Guided Writing (1 lesson) • Nouns • Sentence structures By the end o
Topic 3.7: Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 1

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing, part of Writing 3.6 Guided Writing (1 lesson) • Nouns • Sentence structures By the end o in Grade 5 MANDARIN.

Key inquiry question: How can writing fluency be enhanced?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. underline names of body parts from a list of words collaboratively (e.g. 眼 镜、头、耳 朵、鼻子、嘴巴、手、肚子、角、退、舌 头 etc.),

2. match names of parts of the body with their correct functions from a table (e.g. 眼睛 - 看、腿 - 走、耳朵 - 听、鼻子- 闻),

3. trace out characters on parts of the body and their functions following the correct stroke order (看、子、耳),

4. reconstruct a paragraph with missing or scrambled sentences in a logical and coherent manner,

5. work collaboratively to write a simple poem about parts of the body and their functions,

6. recite the poem for their peers to provide feedback,

7. identify the challenges encountered in their writing and propose solutions or strategies to address them collaboratively.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. underline names of body parts from a list of words collaboratively (e.g. 眼 镜、头、耳 朵、鼻子、嘴巴、手、肚子、角、退、舌 头 etc.),
2. match names of parts of the body with their correct functions from a table (e.g. 眼睛 - 看、腿 - 走、耳朵 - 听、鼻子- 闻),
3. trace out characters on parts of the body and their functions following the correct stroke order (看、子、耳),
4. reconstruct a paragraph with missing or scrambled sentences in a logical and coherent manner,
5. work collaboratively to write a simple poem about parts of the body and their functions,
6. recite the poem for their peers to provide feedback,
7. identify the challenges encountered in their writing and propose solutions or strategies to address them collaboratively.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: Effective communication skills are developed when the learner identifies the challenges in their writing and

proposes strategies to address them.

• Learning to learn: The learner is motivated to learn continuously as they receive constructive feedback from their peers on the

poem.

Values:
Peace: The learner displays calmness as they receive feedback on the simple poem they composed.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Self-awareness: The learner becomes aware of the importance of the different parts of their body and appreciates their functions.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is can link the concept of body parts and their functions to their learning in Science and Technology.
